intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, Praia da Marinha, known for its dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail for panoramic views, then descend to the secluded cove for a refreshing swim. Snorkeling gear can be rented locally to explore the rich marine life.
experiences.location: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Seafood Sunset Tasting
experiences.description: Join a guided wine tasting session at a beachfront restaurant in Albufeira featuring regional Algarve wines such as Vida Nova and Quinta dos Vales paired with fresh local seafood including grilled percebes, amêijoas, and cataplana. Learn about the unique terroir of southern Portugal while watching the sun dip into the Atlantic Ocean.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle by kayak from Praia de Benagil to the world-famous Benagil Cave, a spectacular ocean grotto with a natural skylight opening in its domed ceiling. A guided small-group tour takes you through hidden sea caves and arches along the coastline, offering a unique perspective of the Algarve's iconic rock formations from the water.
experiences.location: Praia de Benagil, Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Quinta dos Vales Vineyard Tour & Tasting
experiences.description: Visit one of the Algarve's premier wineries, Quinta dos Vales, set amid rolling hills near the coast. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of five award-winning wines including their signature Marquês dos Vales Reserva. The estate also features outdoor sculpture gardens and stunning countryside views.
experiences.location: Quinta dos Vales, Estômbar, near Lagoa, Central Algarve

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day with Watersports
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most beautiful sandy beaches in the Algarve stretching over 4 kilometers near Lagos. Rent a sunbed and umbrella, then try windsurfing or stand-up paddleboarding with a local instructor. Wrap up the day with a fresh seafood lunch at one of the beachfront restaurants serving grilled fish and local wines.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport, collect luggage, and take the affordable bus/shuttle to Lagoa (approx. €5–8 via EVA/Rede Expressos). Check in to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay. Take a gentle 10-minute walk down the cliffside trail to iconic Praia da Marinha beach to decompress and enjoy the stunning golden limestone cliffs and turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the cliffside path at sunset for panoramic Algarve views. Head back to the village of Lagoa for a casual first dinner at a local tasca (traditional tavern).

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and coffee at the airport (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Snack from airport or roadside café on arrival route (€4–6)
meals.dinner: Tasca O Zé in Lagoa — try grilled sardines and house wine, budget ~€10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 7-day or 10-trip bus pass from EVA to save on transport. Pick up a local SIM card at Faro Airport (NOS or Vodafone, ~€10–15 with data). September weather is warm (24–28°C) and less crowded than peak summer — perfect timing.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha — arrive before 9:00 AM to enjoy the beach almost entirely to yourself. Explore the sea caves and rock arches accessible by walking along the shoreline at low tide. Bring snorkeling gear if you have it — the water clarity here is exceptional.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi (~€6) to nearby Praia de Benagil. Visit the famous Benagil Sea Cave — book a budget kayak rental (€15–20) or join a shared boat tour (€10–12) to enter the cave from the water. Avoid overpriced private tours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa town center. Browse the weekly market stalls if available. Enjoy a relaxed evening at a local café with a glass of regional Algarve wine.

meals.breakfast: At the accommodation or nearby café — galão (milky coffee) and toast (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Pingo Doce supermarket in Lagoa — bread, local cheese, fruit, and water (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas, Lagoa — cataplana (traditional seafood stew) at ~€12–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave is best visited in the morning for light, but afternoon works well in September. Always check tides before walking sea cave routes. Wear water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus to Carvoeiro (15 min, ~€2). Walk the famous Algar Seco boardwalk — a dramatic cliffside trail with rock formations, natural pools, and sea arches. Free to walk and absolutely stunning in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Praia de Carvoeiro, a small sheltered cove with calm waters perfect for swimming. Explore the whitewashed village of Carvoeiro — browse local craft shops and pick up a handmade ceramic piece as a budget souvenir (€5–10).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the bus back to Lagoa. Visit Adega do Cantor winery tasting room in Guia (short taxi or bus, ~€5–6 away) — owned by Cliff Richard, this local winery offers affordable tastings of Algarve wines (€5–8 for a tasting flight).

meals.breakfast: At accommodation or local padaria (bakery) — croissant and coffee (€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Carvoeiro beach — prego sandwich (beef roll) and beer (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Churrasqueira in Lagoa — grilled chicken piri-piri with chips and salad (€8–10)

day_by_day.notes: Adega do Cantor should be visited by appointment or check opening hours in advance. Alternatively, pick up a bottle of regional Algarve wine at the supermarket (€4–6) for a balcony tasting back at the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the train from Tunes or bus from Lagoa (€2–3). Visit the magnificent Moorish Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves), one of the best-preserved in Portugal. Entry fee ~€3. Explore the red sandstone ramparts with sweeping views over orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Silves old town — visit the Gothic Cathedral (free entry), browse the riverside market area, and walk along the Arade River banks. Stop at a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Silves regional wine (€4–6).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa by bus. Enjoy a relaxed evening with your wine purchase on the hotel terrace or nearby viewpoint watching the sunset over the Algarve hills.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Café Inglês, Silves — atmospheric café inside the castle walls, sandwiches and soup (€7–9)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui, Silves — famous for fresh seafood, budget €12–15 per person with house wine

day_by_day.notes: Silves is the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve — deeply cultural and far less touristy than coastal towns. The Silves Medieval Fair doesn't run in September but the town is still charming. Train connections can be infrequent — check CP (Comboios de Portugal) schedule in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Marinha again at sunrise for golden hour photography — the cliffs glow amber in early light. Take the full 7km Carvoeiro–Marinha cliffside walking trail (free), one of the most beautiful coastal walks in Europe. Start early to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and swim at a quieter cove discovered along the walking trail — Praia de Paraíso or Praia do Carvalho (accessible via steps cut into the cliff). Bring water and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Saturday evening — head into Lagoa town for the lively local atmosphere. Visit the Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa (Lagoa Wine Cooperative), one of the oldest in the Algarve, for an affordable wine tasting (€3–5). Buy a bottle of their acclaimed Afonso III red or white.

meals.breakfast: Pack your own — bread, cheese, fruit from supermarket (€3)
meals.lunch: Picnic on the clifftop trail — charcuterie, local olives, and water (€5–6 from Pingo Doce)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Lagarto, Lagoa — local petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and wine (€10–12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Lagoa Wine Cooperative is a genuine budget gem — their wines win international awards at fraction of boutique winery prices. Saturday evenings in Lagoa are lively with locals — a great cultural experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão — take the bus (€2.50). Visit the Museu de Portimão (Museum of Portimão), a fascinating free or low-cost museum (€3) built inside a former sardine canning factory. Excellent insight into Algarve fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic beach with towering ochre cliffs. Swim and sunbathe. Explore the 16th-century Fortaleza de Santa Catarina at the beach's edge (free to enter the exterior area).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Portimão's riverside promenade (Avenida Guanaré). Watch local fishermen unload their catch. Take the bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Portimão town center — coffee and pastéis (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Sardinha grelhada (grilled sardines) at a riverside tasca in Portimão — €8–10 with bread and salad
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at accommodation using supermarket ingredients — fresh bread, local cheese, cured meats, wine (€6–8 total)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday can be quieter for buses — check EVA timetables the night before. Portimão is a real working fishing city, less touristy than Lagos — great for authentic Algarve culture. September is ideal as beaches are less crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Lagos (€3–4, ~40 min). Explore the historic old town — walk the ancient city walls, visit Igreja de Santo António (small entry fee ~€2), and browse the vibrant Praça Gil Eanes square.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a spectacular headland with dramatic sea stacks, grottoes, and emerald water. Take the staircase down to the water level for free. Optionally rent a kayak locally (€15/hr) to paddle into the sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos's budget-friendly nightlife — the town has many affordable bars popular with backpackers. Try a ginjinha (cherry liqueur) at a local bar (€1.50) and enjoy the lively atmosphere before busing back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: : Nah Nah Bah burger bar, Lagos — great value burgers (€7–9)
meals.dinner: Meu Limão, Lagos — popular budget restaurant, fresh fish dishes €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is the most popular town in western Algarve — go on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. The last bus back to Lagoa/Carvoeiro area typically runs around 20:00–21:00 — confirm times. Ponta da Piedade is free and arguably the most beautiful coastal scenery in all of Portugal.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and slow morning at the hotel. Visit the local Lagoa weekly market (check schedule) for fresh produce, local honey, figs, and almonds — all extremely affordable and quintessentially Algarvian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle from a local shop in Carvoeiro or Lagoa (€10–15/day) and cycle the quiet country roads through the Barrocal — the inland limestone hills dotted with almond, carob, and fig trees. Visit the small village of Estômbar.
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening — visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (book ahead, tastings from €10–15). One of the most acclaimed boutique wineries in the Algarve with stunning sculpture garden.

meals.breakfast: Fresh figs, local bread, and honey from the market (€3–4)
meals.lunch: Snack at a rural café in Estômbar — soup and bread (€4–5)
meals.dinner: Back in Lagoa — Restaurante Henrique Leis area or simple grilled fish at local churrasqueira (€9–11)

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for tastings — contact them a day or two ahead. The inland Barrocal region is completely off the tourist trail and offers an authentic glimpse of traditional Algarve rural life. September means ripe figs everywhere — feel free to pick from roadside trees (common practice).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Albufeira — take the bus (€3, ~30 min). Visit the old town (Albufeira Antiga) early morning before the crowds. Explore the whitewashed lanes, the historic fishermen's tunnel to the beach, and the clifftop church viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) — the original village beach, more charming than the main tourist strip. Swim and relax. Walk east along the cliffs to Praia do Inatel for a quieter spot.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's famous Strip (Avenida Sá Carneiro) for a budget evening drink — many happy hours from 17:00–19:00 with drinks from €2–3. Head back to Lagoa by bus.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Garrett, Albufeira old town — coffee and croissant (€2)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Penedo, Albufeira — fresh grilled fish with view, €10–12
meals.dinner: Back in Lagoa — simple piri-piri chicken takeaway (€7–8)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira is the most touristy town in the Algarve — visit for the old town charm and beaches, but don't feel obligated to stay long if the tourist crowds aren't your style. Morning visits are far more pleasant. The bus connection is reliable and frequent.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the hidden gem of Praia de Vale Centianes — a small, sheltered beach a short walk from Praia da Marinha. Almost completely unknown to tourists, surrounded by dramatic cliffs. Arrive early for total solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Slide & Splash water park in Estômbar (budget option — check for late-season discounts, often €15–20 in September vs €28 peak). Fun afternoon activity if you enjoy water slides, and September crowds are minimal.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Carvoeiro–Marinha cliffs. Pick up a bottle of local wine from the Lagoa Cooperative and enjoy it on the hotel terrace or a clifftop bench.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the beach — tuna sandwiches, fruit, water from supermarket (€4)
meals.dinner: A Ruína, Carvoeiro — affordable seafood restaurant, €11–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Vale Centianes beach requires a short hike down a cliff path — wear good shoes. Slide & Splash is a genuine budget-friendly fun option and nearly empty in mid-September. Check their website for end-of-season deals.

day_by_day.morning: Take a bus to Faro (€5–6, ~1 hour). Visit the Faro old town (Cidade Velha) — walk through the medieval arch (Arco da Vila), visit the beautiful Faro Cathedral (Sé de Faro) with its rooftop terrace (€3.50 entry), and explore the Roman ruins in the garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free ferry (€2.20 round trip) from Faro harbor to Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro — pristine barrier island beaches within the Ria Formosa Natural Park. Crystal clear shallow lagoon water and virtually no development. Perfect for a final big beach day.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro. Browse the pedestrian shopping streets around Rua de Santo António. Take the bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: Bar on Ilha Deserta — fresh grilled fish (€10–12) or pack your own picnic
meals.dinner: Tasca do Bica, Faro old town — traditional Algarvian cuisine, €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Ria Formosa Natural Park is a UNESCO-recognized lagoon ecosystem — one of Portugal's Seven Natural Wonders. The barrier island beaches are arguably the most beautiful and unspoiled in the Algarve. Ferry schedules vary — check at Faro pier on arrival. Last bus back to Lagoa area — confirm by 17:00.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach morning at Praia da Marinha — your home beach and one of the world's most beautiful. Swim, snorkel, and soak in the scenery one last time. Take photos of the famous rock arch from the clifftop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lagoa town center for souvenir shopping — pick up local products: Medronho (arbutus berry spirit, €5–8 a bottle), Algarve honey (€4–6), local almonds and figs (€3–5), and handmade ceramics (€5–15). These are the best value authentic gifts from the region.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on your last night. Visit a slightly nicer local restaurant in Lagoa or Carvoeiro for a proper cataplana feast or grilled sea bass (dourada) with regional wine.

meals.breakfast: At accommodation — full Portuguese breakfast if offered
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia da Marinha — grilled sardine sandwich and local beer (€6–8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo, Carvoeiro — farewell splurge, grilled lobster or cataplana, €18–22 per person (budget treat)

day_by_day.notes: Medronho is the traditional Algarve spirit — buy from local producers at markets or farm shops rather than tourist shops for best prices. Pack your suitcase tonight to make morning departure stress-free. Check bus/transfer times to Faro Airport for tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning — final sunrise walk to the Praia da Marinha clifftop viewpoint for a last look at the golden Algarve coastline. Check out of accommodation. Take bus or pre-booked shuttle to Faro Airport (book in advance for best budget rate — €8–15 via shared shuttle or €5–7 via bus to Faro + taxi).
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. Browse duty-free for any last-minute local wine or port purchases.
day_by_day.evening: Flight home — carry the memories of 13 incredible days on the Algarve coast.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and galão at a Lagoa café before departure (€2–3)
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring snacks from supermarket (€5–8)
meals.dinner: On flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Book airport transfer in advance — GetTransfer, Welcome Pickups, or shared shuttle services offer the best budget rates. Allow at least 2 hours before departure at Faro Airport. Total estimated trip budget breakdown: Accommodation (13 nights budget stay) ~€400–600, Food & drink ~€15–20/day = ~€200–260, Transport (buses, day trips) ~€60–80, Activities & wine tastings ~€80–100, Souvenirs ~€30–50. Estimated total: €770–1,090 for one person — very achievable for a 13-day Algarve trip.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45-minute drive west along the EN125). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your boutique accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a gentle first walk down to Praia da Marinha itself — one of the Algarve's most celebrated beaches. Explore the golden limestone cliffs, sea arches, and crystal-clear turquoise coves. A short coastal path leads to stunning viewpoints. Swim or simply relax and decompress after travel.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro (10-minute drive) for a relaxed first evening. Explore the charming whitewashed streets and watch the sunset from the clifftop boardwalk at Algar Seco.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at the airport or on arrival — light snack to tide you over.
meals.lunch: Pick up a prego (steak roll) or fresh sandwich from a local café near Praia da Marinha after check-in.
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — a reliable mid-range spot with fresh grilled fish, cataplana, and local wines. Budget approx. €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Jet lag and travel fatigue are real — prioritize settling in. Stock up on water and snacks at a local mini-market for the room.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with a leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay, then head out early to explore the Benagil Sea Cave — one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Book a kayak tour or SUP rental from Praia de Benagil (5-minute drive). Paddle into the cathedral-like cave with its famous domed ceiling and interior beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the coastline on a boat tour departing from Benagil or Portimão that covers the dramatic sea caves, grottos, and arches between Lagos and Armação de Pêra. Tours typically last 1.5–2 hours and cost €20–35 per person. Afterward, relax on Praia de Benagil or the quieter Praia do Carvalho.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Lagoa town center (15-minute drive) for the evening. Browse the local market square and enjoy a quiet Portuguese evening.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the boutique stay or a local café — scrambled eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Benagil — grilled sardines, salad, and cold Sagres beer. Budget €12–18.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Praça in Lagoa — a beloved local tasca serving traditional Algarvian dishes like açorda de marisco (seafood bread stew) and grilled dourada. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil kayak or boat tour the day before as September can still be busy. Wear reef shoes if kayaking — the cave entrance can be rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Lagos (30 minutes west) — one of the Algarve's most charming historic towns. Explore the old town walls, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), and the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning gilded baroque interior. Walk the cobblestone lanes and admire the azulejo-tiled facades.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Lagos's famous beaches — Praia Dona Ana, Praia do Camilo, or the dramatic Ponta da Piedade headland with its towering golden rock formations. Rent a kayak or join a boat tour from the marina to explore the sea caves and arches up close. Spend the rest of the afternoon swimming and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner and evening drinks. The waterfront Avenida dos Descobrimentos and the pedestrian Rua 25 de Abril are lively with restaurants and bars.

meals.breakfast: Café Correia or similar local pastelaria in Lagos old town — coffee, croissant, and fresh orange juice.
meals.lunch: : A Forja restaurant in Lagos — a no-frills, excellent-value spot popular with locals. Try the grilled lulas (squid) or bifanas. Budget €12–18.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos — overlooking the marina, great for fresh seafood cataplana and regional wines. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon light for photography. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the cliff steps down to the rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a wine tasting experience. Drive to the Algarve wine region around Lagoa — visit Adega Cooperativa do Algarve or Quinta dos Vales (near Estômbar, 15 minutes from the hotel). Both offer guided cellar tours and tastings of local Algarve DOC wines including Negra Mole and Crato Branco varieties. Tours typically cost €10–20 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the wine tasting, head to the nearby Silves town (20 minutes north of Lagoa). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves — the best-preserved Moorish castle in Portugal. Walk the ramparts for panoramic views over the orange groves and countryside. Visit the Gothic Sé Cathedral below.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Silves before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay — fuel up before the wine tasting.
meals.lunch: Light cheese and charcuterie snacks included with the wine tasting, or grab a sandwich in Lagoa before heading to Silves.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — a legendary local institution famous for cataplana de marisco and grilled fish. Slightly splurge-worthy. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Designate a non-drinking driver for the wine tasting morning, or arrange a taxi/Uber. Quinta dos Vales also has beautiful sculpture gardens worth exploring.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the western Algarve's wild coastline — drive to Sagres (1 hour west) and visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres, a 15th-century fortress perched on a windswept headland at Europe's southwestern tip. Walk the clifftops, see the mysterious giant wind compass (Rosa dos Ventos), and take in the raw Atlantic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Sagres, drive 6km to Cabo de São Vicente — the most southwesterly point of continental Europe. The lighthouse and cliffs are spectacular. Then head to Praia do Beliche or Praia da Mareta in Sagres for a swim in the cooler Atlantic waters. The surf here is world-class — consider a beginner surf lesson with a local school (€35–45).
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the hotel via the scenic EN268 road through the Costa Vicentina natural park. Stop in Aljezur or Vila do Bispo for a quick browse before heading home.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the boutique stay before the drive.
meals.lunch: A Tasca in Sagres or Restaurante O Telheiro do Infante — fresh tuna steak or grilled sea bass with ocean views. Budget €18–25.
meals.dinner: Back near Carvoeiro — try Restaurante O Pátio in Carvoeiro for a relaxed evening with grilled meats and local wines. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light layer. The drive along the Costa Vicentina is breathtaking and largely undeveloped — a complete contrast to the eastern Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning — enjoy a beach day closer to home. Walk the coastal footpath (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos) from Praia de Vale Covo toward Praia do Carvalho. This 5km clifftop trail passes seven suspended valleys and some of the most dramatic coastal scenery in the Algarve. Take your time and swim at hidden cove beaches along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Praia da Marinha for the afternoon. Rent a paddleboard or snorkel in the clear waters around the rock formations. The underwater caves and marine life here are exceptional. Alternatively, simply relax on the beach with a good book.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ferragudo village (20 minutes east) — a charming, less-touristed fishing village on the Arade River estuary. Walk along the riverfront, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João do Arade, and enjoy the golden evening light.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Carvoeiro before the trail — coffee and a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local supermarket for the coastal trail.
meals.dinner: Sueste Restaurant in Ferragudo — beloved waterfront restaurant with excellent fresh fish and seafood rice. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys trail is well-marked but has uneven terrain — wear proper walking shoes. Bring sun protection, water, and a hat. The trail is best done early before the midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Faro — the Algarve's capital (1 hour drive). Start with the atmospheric Cidade Velha (Old Town) — walk through the Arco da Vila into the cathedral square. Climb the Sé de Faro bell tower for panoramic views over the Ria Formosa lagoon. Visit the hauntingly beautiful Igreja dos Ossos (Chapel of Bones) in the Igreja do Carmo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry from Faro harbor into the Ria Formosa Natural Park — a stunning lagoon system of barrier islands, salt marshes, and tidal flats. Visit Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) or Ilha de Faro for an afternoon of swimming in calm, warm lagoon waters. Ferry tickets cost €10–15 return.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's pedestrian center — Rua de Santo António — before dinner. Browse local ceramics and cork goods shops.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Garret in Faro old town — excellent pastéis de nata and bica coffee.
meals.lunch: Picnic on Ilha Deserta or snack at the small beach bar on the island.
meals.dinner: Tasca do Ricky in Faro — a cozy, popular local restaurant with excellent amêijoas à bulhão pato (clams) and grilled fish. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Faro is often overlooked by tourists who fly straight through — it's well worth a full day. The Ria Formosa is a UNESCO-protected ecosystem and one of Portugal's most important natural parks.

day_by_day.morning: Second wine tasting experience — drive to the Tavira/Tavira region or stay local and visit Quinta da Penina or Herdade dos Pimenteiros near Silves. Alternatively, visit Quinta do Francês in Silves for an intimate small-producer tasting focusing on organic Algarve wines. Pair the tasting with a light tour of the vineyard and winery.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tasting, drive to Portimão (20 minutes) and explore the Museu de Portimão — a fascinating free museum built inside a former sardine canning factory, telling the story of the region's fishing and canning heritage. Then walk along the Portimão riverfront and browse the marina.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for dinner — the city has a vibrant restaurant scene along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Snacks at the winery or a café near Silves.
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão — excellent sardines, grilled fish, and regional wines in a casual riverside setting. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Portimão's Museu is free and surprisingly excellent — allow 1.5 hours. The sardine grilling along the waterfront in Portimão is a local institution.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the hinterland — drive north into the Serra de Monchique mountains (45 minutes from the hotel). Visit the spa town of Caldas de Monchique, a beautifully preserved 19th-century thermal spa village nestled in a wooded valley. Walk the shaded paths, taste the famous mineral water, and browse local medronho (arbutus berry brandy) producers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up to Fóia — the highest peak in the Algarve at 902m. On clear days, views extend to both the Atlantic and the Guadiana River on the Spanish border. Explore the village of Monchique itself — wander the steep cobblestone streets and visit the Igreja Matriz with its unusual Manueline doorway.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the coast via the scenic mountain road. Stop at a miradouro (viewpoint) for sunset over the Algarve coastline spread below.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the mountain drive.
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — traditional mountain cuisine including roast lamb, chouriço, and local cheeses. Budget €15–22.
meals.dinner: Back near Carvoeiro — Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro for a relaxed dinner of grilled fish and local white wine. Budget €22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique is dramatically different from the coastal Algarve — lush, green, and cool. Bring a light jacket. Buy a bottle of medronho as a souvenir — it's the local spirit.

day_by_day.morning: Beach exploration day — drive east to discover some of the Algarve's less-visited beaches. Start at Praia de Armação de Pêra (20 minutes east), a long sandy beach backed by a historic fortified chapel. Then continue to Praia de Albufeira and the dramatic Praia de São Rafael with its extraordinary rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Albufeira old town — despite its party reputation, the historic Moorish quarter (Bairro dos Pescadores) is genuinely charming. Walk the old fishermen's quarter, see the Igreja de São Sebastião, and browse the clifftop promenade. Take the tunnel to the main beach for a late afternoon swim.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's old town for dinner and evening drinks — the Rua Cândido dos Reis has a good mix of lively and quieter options.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast near Armação de Pêra — fresh orange juice and a torrada.
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Praia de São Rafael — grilled chicken piri-piri and salad. Budget €12–16.
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira old town — a historic restaurant built into the old town ruins with excellent fresh fish. Budget €28–38 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be touristy but the old town retains genuine Portuguese character. Avoid the 'strip' area (Avenida Dr. Francisco Sá Carneiro) which is more nightclub territory.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated beach and water sports morning at Praia da Marinha. Book a stand-up paddleboard session, snorkeling tour, or coasteering experience with a local operator. The limestone rock formations and underwater caves around Marinha are perfect for exploring. Alternatively, join a dolphin watching boat trip departing from Portimão or Lagos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Silves for the afternoon — this time focus on the charming town itself rather than the castle. Visit the Museu Arqueológico de Silves (built over an ancient Moorish cistern), browse the weekly market if it's running, and walk along the Arade River banks lined with orange and lemon trees.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Carvoeiro. The Algar Seco clifftop area has a bar with extraordinary views. Then dinner in Carvoeiro village.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay.
meals.lunch: Café do Rio in Silves — riverside café with light lunches, salads, and cold drinks. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: O Castelo Restaurant in Carvoeiro — try the cataplana de peixe (fish cataplana) for two, a traditional Algarvian copper pot dish. Budget €25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin watching trips (€35–50) are best booked in advance. September still has good dolphin sightings. The coasteering experience is a highlight — jumping from cliffs into the sea with a guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final full wine and gastronomy experience — visit a local market (Mercado de Lagoa on Saturday mornings if applicable) for fresh regional produce — local cheeses, honey, carob products, fresh figs, and almonds. Then visit a local wine shop or deli in Lagoa for a self-guided tasting and to pick up bottles to bring home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last big beach afternoon — return to your favorite beach from the trip, or try Praia do Carvalho (a hidden gem accessible only through a tunnel in the cliffs near Carvoeiro). Swim, sunbathe, and soak up the last full afternoon of Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a special meal to mark the last evening.

meals.breakfast: Market breakfast — fresh bread, local cheese, and fruit bought at the market.
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with market produce and local wine.
meals.dinner: Splurge dinner at Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande (near Portimão) — one of the Algarve's most celebrated traditional restaurants, famous for cataplana and regional cuisine. Reserve ahead. Budget €40–55 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Buy wine, medronho, local honey, and almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos, Morgados) as gifts and souvenirs. Pack purchases carefully for the flight home.

day_by_day.morning: Slow, relaxed final morning. Pack, check out of the boutique stay. Take one last walk down to Praia da Marinha to say goodbye to the cliffs and sea. Grab a final coffee and pastel de nata at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (allow 50–60 minutes from Praia da Marinha). Return rental car if applicable. Enjoy a final bica (espresso) at the airport. Depart Portugal.
day_by_day.evening: In transit — homeward bound with a suitcase full of wine, local sweets, and 13 days of golden Algarve memories.

meals.breakfast: Final Portuguese breakfast at a café near the hotel — coffee, fresh orange juice, and a warm pastel de nata.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport or a café in Faro if time allows before the flight.
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time at Faro Airport in September as it can be busy with returning holiday traffic. Check baggage restrictions if carrying wine bottles — wrap them well or use a wine travel bag.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from Faro Airport to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45 min). Enjoy a chilled welcome drink and private check-in experience upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a leisurely first exploration of the iconic Praia da Marinha beach, just steps from the boutique stay. Stroll along the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, discover hidden sea caves, and soak in the turquoise Atlantic waters. This UNESCO-recognized coastline is one of Portugal's most photographed — a perfect gentle introduction.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace or clifftop viewpoint overlooking the Atlantic. Enjoy a glass of local Algarve Vinho Verde or Cava as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the boutique stay upon arrival — charcuterie, local cheeses, fresh bread, and regional olives paired with chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vila Joya (2 Michelin stars, Albufeira, ~20 min drive) — one of Portugal's most celebrated fine dining restaurants. Book the chef's tasting menu featuring modern interpretations of Portuguese coastal cuisine with an exceptional wine pairing program

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Vila Joya requires reservations well ahead — book at least 2–3 months prior. Day 1 is intentionally relaxed to allow for jet lag recovery and acclimatization.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided boat tour departing from Benagil Beach (10 min drive). Explore the world-famous Benagil Sea Cave, hidden grottoes, and secluded golden beaches only accessible by sea. Opt for a premium private catamaran charter for an exclusive experience with chilled Champagne and fresh fruit on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Carvalho and Praia do Paraíso — two of the Algarve's most secluded and pristine beaches reachable by a short coastal walk. Bring a luxury beach hamper arranged by the hotel (chilled rosé, artisan sandwiches, local pastries). Spend the afternoon swimming in crystal-clear coves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a private in-villa spa treatment — book a couples' massage or a traditional Portuguese-inspired body ritual using local cork and argan oils.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — fresh pastries, local honey, smoked salmon, eggs to order, and freshly squeezed orange juice from Algarve oranges
meals.lunch: Luxury beach picnic hamper prepared by the hotel — chilled Alvarinho white wine, grilled octopus salad, artisan cheeses, and local pastéis de nata
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Sueste in Ferragudo (~15 min drive) — an elegant waterfront restaurant renowned for impeccably fresh seafood. Try the grilled whole sea bass and Algarve tiger prawns paired with a crisp Arinto from Setúbal

day_by_day.notes: Book private boat charter at least 48 hours in advance. September waters are warm (22–24°C) and ideal for swimming. Benagil cave is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Private wine tasting experience at Adega do Cantor (Guia, ~25 min drive) — the winery founded by Cliff Richard, producing award-winning Algarve wines. Enjoy a guided cellar tour, barrel tasting, and a curated flight of their premium reds, whites, and rosés with a sommelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic town of Silves (~30 min drive) — the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the imposing red sandstone Castelo de Silves with panoramic views, and wander the cobblestone streets lined with orange trees. Visit the Gothic Cathedral and the Regional Archaeology Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at the hotel followed by a private chef dinner experience at the boutique stay — arrange for a local chef to prepare a traditional cataplana feast (a slow-cooked copper pot dish of clams, chorizo, and vegetables) exclusively for your party.

meals.breakfast: Hotel gourmet breakfast with açorda (traditional Portuguese bread soup) option alongside continental selections
meals.lunch: Wine and cheese pairing lunch at Adega do Cantor winery — regional charcuterie, aged queijo de cabra (goat cheese), fig jam, and Algarve almonds
meals.dinner: Private in-villa chef experience — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana), grilled Algarve figs with prosciutto starter, and a decadent pastel de amêndoa (almond tart) for dessert, paired with wines selected by your sommelier

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private chef through the boutique stay concierge at least 2 days in advance. Adega do Cantor tastings should be pre-booked. Silves is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga session on the clifftop overlooking Praia da Marinha, led by a personal instructor arranged through the hotel. Follow with a refreshing sea dip at the beach below. The September morning light on the limestone cliffs is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (~1.5 hrs) — the dramatic southwestern tip of continental Europe. Tour the historic Fortaleza de Sagres, walk the windswept cliffs, and experience the raw, elemental beauty of this legendary cape where Portuguese explorers once set sail. Visit the lighthouse at Cabo de São Vicente.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at Cabo de São Vicente watching the sunset over the Atlantic — one of the most dramatic sunsets in all of Europe. Drive back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga breakfast of fresh fruit, Greek yogurt with local honey, and herbal tea. Full breakfast upon return from the beach
meals.lunch: Lunch at Memmo Baleeira Hotel restaurant in Sagres — fresh catch of the day, grilled to perfection, with panoramic ocean views. Pair with a chilled Alvarinho
meals.dinner: Dinner at O Leão de Portimão (~20 min from hotel) — a sophisticated riverside restaurant in Portimão specializing in premium grilled fish and Algarve specialties. Try the grilled turbot and finish with Dom Rodrigo (traditional Algarve almond and egg sweet)

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is a longer drive — depart by 11:30 AM after breakfast. The cape can be windy; bring a light layer. September sunsets at Cabo de São Vicente are typically spectacular. Book restaurant in advance for Friday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Private stand-up paddleboard (SUP) or kayak tour along the Marinha coastline with a certified guide. Paddle through sea arches, into hidden caves, and along the base of the golden cliffs — a perspective of the Algarve coast that few visitors experience. Includes snorkeling stop at a secluded cove.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming village of Carvoeiro (~15 min drive) — a picturesque fishing village with whitewashed houses cascading down to a small golden beach. Browse the artisan boutiques, visit the Algar Seco rock formations (a dramatic coastal promenade), and enjoy the relaxed village atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar in Carvoeiro followed by a premium dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast with made-to-order omelets, smoked Algarve fish, fresh pastries, and local fruit platters
meals.lunch: Post-water-sports lunch at Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro — grilled seafood, fresh salads, and cold Sagres beer or local white wine on a sun-drenched terrace
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Três Palmeiras in Portimão (~20 min) — an iconic fine dining institution perched above the ocean, renowned for whole grilled fish, lobster, and exceptional wine list. Request a window table for Atlantic views

day_by_day.notes: Book SUP/kayak tour through the hotel concierge. Algar Seco is best visited in the afternoon when tour groups have thinned. Saturday evenings in Carvoeiro are lively — enjoy the village ambiance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wine and food heritage tour of the Lagoa wine region — the heart of Algarve wine production. Visit Quinta dos Vales (~20 min drive), a premium estate winery with stunning sculpture gardens. Enjoy a private cellar tour, barrel tasting, and guided walk through the vineyards with the estate sommelier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to a second premium winery — Quinta da Penina or Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — for a comparative tasting of Algarve's indigenous grape varieties including Negra Mole, Crato Branco, and Perrum. Explore the differences between the region's terroir zones.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Private in-room wine and cheese board arranged by the hotel — curated selection of the day's favorites alongside premium Portuguese cheeses from Serra da Estrela and Azeitão.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely Sunday hotel breakfast — full spread including freshly baked bread, local jams, cold cuts, eggs Benedict, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Winery lunch at Quinta dos Vales — estate-prepared spread of regional dishes paired with their award-winning wines in the vineyard setting
meals.dinner: Relaxed in-room or hotel terrace dining — premium cheese and charcuterie board with wines from the day's tastings, accompanied by local honey, figs, and artisan crackers

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales requires advance booking for private tours. September is harvest season in the Algarve — there may be an opportunity to participate in a grape harvest activity at the winery. Confirm with the estate in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro (~1 hr drive). Board a private boat charter to explore the stunning lagoon ecosystem — a mosaic of islands, salt marshes, tidal flats, and barrier islands. Visit the car-free islands of Ilha Deserta or Ilha do Farol for pristine, uncrowded beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon on Ilha Deserta — arguably the most pristine beach in the Algarve. The island has just one restaurant (Estaminé) and miles of untouched sand. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the extraordinary tranquility. The September crowds are minimal.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to the mainland. Drive back toward Lagoa. Optional stop in Faro's historic old town (Cidade Velha) for a brief evening stroll through the medieval walls and cathedral square.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — lighter option of fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, croissants, and coffee before the drive to Faro
meals.lunch: Lunch at Estaminé restaurant on Ilha Deserta — the island's only dining option, serving exceptionally fresh seafood and fish caught that morning, with stunning views of the lagoon
meals.dinner: Dinner at Faro's acclaimed Restaurante 2 Passos (~5 min from Faro old town) — sophisticated Portuguese cuisine with creative tasting menus, excellent wine list, and intimate atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private boat charter through Faro-based operators in advance. Ilha Deserta has no shade — bring sun protection, hats, and plenty of water. Estaminé is the only restaurant on the island; book ahead even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Private golf experience at Penina Hotel & Golf Resort (~25 min drive) — one of the Algarve's most prestigious championship golf courses, designed by Sir Henry Cotton. Enjoy a round on the Championship Course with a private caddy. Non-golfers can enjoy the resort's luxury spa and pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Lunch and spa afternoon at Penina Resort. Indulge in the full spa menu — hydrotherapy circuit, traditional hammam, and a 90-minute signature massage using Portuguese marine-inspired products.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lagos (~35 min from hotel) for an evening exploring one of the Algarve's most beautiful historic towns. Walk the ancient city walls, visit the Ponta da Piedade rock formations at dusk, and browse the atmospheric old town.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel gourmet breakfast — fuel up for the golf morning with a protein-rich spread
meals.lunch: Post-golf lunch at Penina's signature restaurant — club sandwiches, fresh salads, and cold drinks on the terrace overlooking the fairways
meals.dinner: Dinner at Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — a beloved upscale restaurant serving creative takes on traditional Algarve recipes. Try the black pork secretos and the cataplana de lingueirão (razor clam cataplana)

day_by_day.notes: Book golf tee time at Penina well in advance — September is still peak golf season. Spa treatments should also be pre-booked. Ponta da Piedade in Lagos is best at sunset — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided jeep safari through the Algarve's interior — the Serra de Monchique mountain range (~45 min from hotel). Explore the lush eucalyptus and cork oak forests, visit the thermal spa town of Caldas de Monchique, and hike to the summit of Fóia (902m) — the highest point in the Algarve — for panoramic views stretching to the Atlantic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Monchique — a hillside market town famous for its medronho (arbutus berry firewater) and local crafts. Visit an artisan medronho distillery for a private tasting. Browse the local market for handmade cork products, ceramics, and local preserves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel. Relaxed evening with a private outdoor dinner on the hotel terrace or garden.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before the jeep safari departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Luar da Fóia in Monchique — a rustic mountain restaurant with spectacular views, serving hearty Algarve interior cuisine: roasted black pork, smoked sausages, and local bean stews
meals.dinner: Private terrace dinner at the boutique stay — hotel-arranged premium dining experience featuring a curated menu of Algarve coastal and mountain specialties, paired with wines from the Lagoa region

day_by_day.notes: The Serra de Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast — bring a light jacket. The medronho distillery visit should be arranged in advance through the hotel concierge. September foliage in the mountains is lush and beautiful.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private catamaran charter departing from Portimão marina (~20 min drive). Sail westward along the Algarve's most dramatic coastline — past Praia da Marinha, Benagil, and toward Sagres. Swim in secluded bays, snorkel over underwater rock formations, and enjoy the deck with Champagne and fresh seafood prepared on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the catamaran journey — anchor at a remote beach for a private beach picnic. Swim, kayak from the boat, or simply relax on deck with the crew attending to every need. Dolphin sightings are common in September along this stretch of coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Portimão marina at sunset. Freshen up and enjoy the evening in Portimão's riverside dining district.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast before departure to the marina
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-board lunch prepared by the catamaran chef — grilled fresh fish, chilled seafood platters, Algarve olives, and chilled Alvarinho white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Vista in Portimão (Bela Vista Hotel) — a Michelin-starred restaurant with stunning river views, offering a sophisticated tasting menu celebrating Algarve's finest ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Full-day private catamaran charter must be booked well in advance. Confirm the on-board chef option when booking. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, and light layers for the sea breeze. Vista restaurant requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided cultural tour of Tavira (~1.5 hrs drive east) — widely considered the most elegant and romantic town in the Algarve. Explore the Roman bridge, the castle ruins, and the extraordinary collection of 37 churches. Visit the Misericórdia Church with its stunning Renaissance portal and gilded azulejo-tiled interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short boat ferry to Ilha de Tavira — a barrier island with one of the Algarve's finest and most unspoiled beaches. Spend the afternoon on the vast, tranquil sands. The September sea is warm and the beach is significantly quieter than summer months.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tavira for an evening stroll along the Gilão River promenade. Enjoy the golden-hour light on the whitewashed buildings before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before the drive to Tavira
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quatro Águas restaurant in Tavira — a legendary seafood restaurant overlooking the Ria Formosa lagoon, famous for its fresh oysters, clams, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante Aquasul in Tavira — a sophisticated restaurant in a beautifully restored townhouse, offering refined Algarve cuisine with an exceptional wine cellar. Try the tuna tataki with algae and the slow-roasted lamb

day_by_day.notes: Tavira is a longer drive — plan to depart by 9:30 AM. The town is best explored on foot. Ilha de Tavira ferry runs regularly from Quatro Águas dock. September is an ideal time — warm but not crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day at Praia da Marinha — your home beach for the trip. Arrange for the hotel to set up a premium beach cabana with sun loungers, chilled towels, and a personal beach butler. Swim in the crystal-clear September waters one last time and explore the coastal rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a luxurious farewell spa afternoon — full body treatment, facial, and relaxation in the hotel's wellness facilities. Alternatively, enjoy a final private wine tasting at the hotel — a curated retrospective of the best wines experienced during the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant of the trip — a celebratory final evening in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the hotel terrace — a special send-off with fresh oysters, smoked salmon, pastries, and a bottle of Algarve sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch — hotel-prepared hamper with chilled gazpacho, grilled chicken wraps, fresh fruit, and rosé wine enjoyed at the beach cabana
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner at Vila Joya (return visit, 2 Michelin stars) — the full chef's tasting menu with premium wine pairing, celebrating the end of an extraordinary Algarve journey

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the beach cabana setup the night before through the hotel. Vila Joya farewell dinner should be booked in advance. Consider purchasing a selection of local wines, medronho, and artisan products to bring home — ask the hotel concierge for assistance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — a slow, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Pack and prepare for departure. Take one last walk along the Praia da Marinha cliffs to say farewell to the extraordinary Algarve coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Praia da Marinha, Lagoa to Faro Airport. Allow ample time for the 45-minute journey. Enjoy a final pastel de nata and bica (espresso) at the airport before departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final leisurely gourmet hotel breakfast — order everything you loved during the stay. Savor the last Algarve oranges, local honey, and freshly baked pastries
meals.lunch: Light airport lunch or snacks — or stop en route at a local pastelaria for a final authentic Portuguese experience
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private transfer the night before. Check out procedures should be confirmed with the hotel in advance. Consider tipping the hotel staff who made the stay exceptional. Allow at least 2.5 hours before flight departure for the transfer and airport procedures.
